questions.stem: A 44-year-old man with moderate persistent asthma started a new oral asthma drug 2 months ago, taken several times a day. He now has fatigue and mild discomfort in the right upper abdomen. He drinks no alcohol and takes no other medicines. Viral hepatitis serologies are negative. Laboratory results: ALT 312 U/L (normal under 40), AST 238 U/L (normal under 40), alkaline phosphatase 96 U/L (normal) and total bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL (normal). The enzymes return to normal after the drug is stopped. What was the mechanism of the drug he was taking?
choices: Blockade of the cysteinyl leukotriene receptor
questions.explanation: A hepatocellular pattern of injury (high aminotransferases, normal alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin) with an oral asthma drug taken several times a day points to **zileuton**, which inhibits **5-lipoxygenase** and is known for **hepatotoxicity**, so liver enzymes are monitored. Montelukast also acts on the leukotriene pathway, but it blocks the receptor, is taken once daily and only rarely injures the liver. Cromolyn is inhaled, and theophylline toxicity causes vomiting, arrhythmias and seizures rather than hepatitis. Roflumilast (PDE-4 inhibition) is used in COPD, not asthma, and is not hepatotoxic.
questions.explanation_pt: Um padrão de lesão hepatocelular (aminotransferases altas, fosfatase alcalina e bilirrubina normais) com um fármaco oral para asma tomado várias vezes ao dia aponta para a **zileutona**, que inibe a **5-lipoxigenase** e é conhecida pela **hepatotoxicidade**, por isso as enzimas hepáticas são monitoradas. O montelucaste também atua na via dos leucotrienos, mas bloqueia o receptor, é tomado uma vez ao dia e só raramente lesa o fígado. O cromoglicato é inalatório, e a toxicidade da teofilina causa vômitos, arritmias e convulsões, e não hepatite. O roflumilaste (inibição da PDE-4) é usado na DPOC, não na asma, e não é hepatotóxico.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman with COPD has taken the same dose of oral theophylline for 2 years with stable serum levels. She smoked 30 cigarettes a day until 3 weeks ago, when she stopped and began using a nicotine patch. She takes no new drugs. She now has nausea, poor sleep, a fine tremor and palpitations. Pulse is 116/min. Her serum theophylline level is clearly higher than at her last visit. Which mechanism best explains the rise?
choices: Loss of hepatic CYP1A2 induction by compounds in tobacco smoke
Inhibition of hepatic CYP1A2 by nicotine from the patch
Reduced renal excretion of theophylline after smoking stops
Greater intestinal absorption of theophylline after smoking stops
Displacement of theophylline from albumin by nicotine
questions.explanation: **Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons** in tobacco smoke **induce CYP1A2**, the main enzyme that clears theophylline. When she stops smoking, the induction fades over days to weeks, clearance falls, and the same dose produces a higher level with signs of **theophylline toxicity**. The nicotine patch is the tempting answer, but nicotine itself neither induces nor inhibits CYP1A2; the inducers are the combustion products, which the patch does not deliver.
questions.explanation_pt: Os **hidrocarbonetos aromáticos policíclicos** da fumaça do tabaco **induzem o CYP1A2**, a principal enzima que elimina a teofilina. Quando ela para de fumar, a indução desaparece em dias a semanas, a depuração cai e a mesma dose gera um nível mais alto, com sinais de **toxicidade da teofilina**. O adesivo de nicotina é a resposta tentadora, mas a nicotina em si não induz nem inibe o CYP1A2; os indutores são os produtos da combustão, que o adesivo não fornece.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man with severe COPD of the chronic bronchitis type has a productive cough on most days. He has had three exacerbations in the past year even though he uses a long-acting muscarinic antagonist and a long-acting beta-2 agonist correctly. His physician adds a once-daily oral tablet. It is a weak bronchodilator; its main effect is to raise cAMP inside neutrophils and other inflammatory cells by blocking one specific isoform of the enzyme that breaks cAMP down. Weight loss and diarrhea are common adverse effects. Which drug was added?
questions.explanation: **Roflumilast** selectively inhibits **phosphodiesterase-4**, the main cAMP-degrading isoform in inflammatory cells. It lowers airway inflammation and reduces exacerbations in **COPD with chronic bronchitis**; **weight loss**, diarrhea, nausea and insomnia are typical adverse effects. Theophylline also raises cAMP, but it inhibits phosphodiesterases nonselectively, blocks adenosine receptors and has a narrow therapeutic index with arrhythmias and seizures in toxicity.
questions.explanation_pt: O **roflumilaste** inibe seletivamente a **fosfodiesterase-4**, a principal isoforma que degrada o AMPc nas células inflamatórias. Reduz a inflamação das vias aéreas e as exacerbações na **DPOC com bronquite crônica**; **perda de peso**, diarreia, náuseas e insônia são efeitos adversos típicos. A teofilina também aumenta o AMPc, mas inibe as fosfodiesterases de forma não seletiva, bloqueia receptores de adenosina e tem índice terapêutico estreito, com arritmias e convulsões na intoxicação.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman takes sertraline for depression. For 2 days she has used large amounts of an over-the-counter cough and cold syrup for a dry cough. She is brought to the emergency department because she is restless and confused. Vital signs: temperature 39.1°C (102.4°F), pulse 124/min, blood pressure 158/94 mm Hg and respirations 22/min. She is sweating heavily and has dilated pupils, diarrhea, hyperactive bowel sounds, brisk reflexes and inducible clonus at both ankles. Which ingredient of the syrup most likely caused this reaction?
questions.explanation: Fever, agitation, **sweating**, diarrhea, **hyperreflexia** and **clonus** in a patient taking an SSRI is **serotonin syndrome**. **Dextromethorphan**, a central antitussive, inhibits serotonin reuptake, so it adds to sertraline. Diphenhydramine is tempting because anticholinergic toxicity also causes fever, tachycardia, confusion and dilated pupils, but it produces dry skin, absent bowel sounds and no clonus. Pseudoephedrine and phenylephrine can raise blood pressure but do not cause clonus.
questions.explanation_pt: Febre, agitação, **sudorese**, diarreia, **hiper-reflexia** e **clônus** em paciente que usa um ISRS caracterizam a **síndrome serotoninérgica**. O **dextrometorfano**, um antitussígeno central, inibe a recaptação de serotonina e assim soma seu efeito ao da sertralina. A difenidramina é tentadora porque a intoxicação anticolinérgica também causa febre, taquicardia, confusão e midríase, mas produz pele seca, ruídos hidroaéreos ausentes e nenhum clônus. A pseudoefedrina e a fenilefrina podem elevar a pressão arterial, mas não causam clônus.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man with early COPD wants to stop smoking. He has had two generalized seizures after a head injury and now takes levetiracetam. He has failed nicotine patches before. His physician chooses a tablet that eases craving and withdrawal and also makes smoking less rewarding if he lights a cigarette, and avoids a different option because of his seizure history. What is the mechanism of the chosen drug?
choices: Inhibition of dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake
Partial agonism at α4β2 nicotinic receptors
Full agonism at α4β2 nicotinic receptors
questions.explanation: **Varenicline** is a **partial agonist** at **α4β2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors**: it releases some dopamine to ease craving and withdrawal, and it occupies the receptor so nicotine from a cigarette gives less reward. Bupropion, which inhibits dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake, is the tempting choice, but it **lowers the seizure threshold** and should be avoided in a patient with seizures. Full nicotinic agonism describes nicotine replacement, which he has already failed.
questions.explanation_pt: A **vareniclina** é um **agonista parcial** dos **receptores nicotínicos α4β2**: libera um pouco de dopamina, aliviando a fissura e a abstinência, e ocupa o receptor, de modo que a nicotina do cigarro dá menos recompensa. A bupropiona, que inibe a recaptação de dopamina e noradrenalina, é a opção tentadora, mas **reduz o limiar convulsivo** e deve ser evitada em paciente com convulsões. O agonismo nicotínico pleno corresponde à reposição de nicotina, que já falhou.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman with chronic bronchitis brings up thick, sticky sputum that she can hardly clear. Her physician prescribes a nebulized drug whose free sulfhydryl group acts directly on the mucus. She is warned that the inhaled drug can trigger bronchospasm and has an unpleasant smell. How does this drug make the sputum thinner?
choices: It cleaves extracellular DNA released by neutrophils
It increases the open time of CFTR chloride channels
It blocks M3 receptors on submucosal glands
It increases the water content of airway secretions
It breaks disulfide bonds that link mucin proteins
questions.explanation: **N-acetylcysteine** has a free **thiol (sulfhydryl) group** that breaks the **disulfide bonds** cross-linking mucin glycoproteins, so mucus becomes less viscous; inhaled, it can cause **bronchospasm**, so it is often given with a bronchodilator. Cleavage of extracellular DNA is the action of **dornase alfa**, which works mainly on the DNA-rich purulent sputum of cystic fibrosis. Guaifenesin is the expectorant thought to increase the water content of secretions, and ivacaftor potentiates CFTR.
questions.explanation_pt: A **N-acetilcisteína** tem um grupo **tiol (sulfidrila)** livre que quebra as **pontes dissulfeto** entre as glicoproteínas da mucina, tornando o muco menos viscoso; por via inalatória pode causar **broncoespasmo**, por isso costuma ser dada com um broncodilatador. A clivagem do DNA extracelular é a ação da **alfadornase**, que age sobretudo no escarro purulento rico em DNA da fibrose cística. A guaifenesina é o expectorante que aumentaria o conteúdo de água das secreções, e o ivacaftor potencializa o CFTR.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman has severe asthma that started in adulthood. She needed three courses of oral prednisone last year despite high-dose inhaled corticosteroid plus a long-acting beta-2 agonist used correctly. Skin prick tests to common aeroallergens are negative. Laboratory results: leukocyte count 7,100/mm3 with 12% eosinophils (absolute eosinophil count about 850/mm3) and total serum IgE 48 IU/mL (normal). Her physician starts a monoclonal antibody that neutralizes the cytokine most needed for eosinophil maturation and survival. Which drug was started?
questions.explanation: Severe adult-onset asthma with high blood **eosinophils**, negative allergy tests and normal IgE is **eosinophilic, non-allergic asthma**. **IL-5** drives eosinophil maturation, activation and survival, and **mepolizumab** binds IL-5. Omalizumab is the tempting answer, but it binds free IgE and is used in allergic asthma with sensitization and raised IgE. Dupilumab blocks the IL-4 receptor alpha chain (IL-4 and IL-13), not IL-5.
questions.explanation_pt: Asma grave de início na idade adulta, com **eosinófilos** altos no sangue, testes alérgicos negativos e IgE normal, é **asma eosinofílica não alérgica**. A **IL-5** promove a maturação, a ativação e a sobrevida dos eosinófilos, e o **mepolizumabe** se liga à IL-5. O omalizumabe é a resposta tentadora, mas se liga à IgE livre e é usado na asma alérgica com sensibilização e IgE elevada. O dupilumabe bloqueia a cadeia alfa do receptor de IL-4 (IL-4 e IL-13), e não a IL-5.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension has dyspnea at rest and signs of right heart failure. She starts a continuous intravenous infusion through a tunneled central catheter and a portable pump. Over the next weeks she notes facial flushing, headache, diarrhea and jaw pain when she starts to eat. She is told that a sudden stop of the infusion can cause dangerous rebound pulmonary hypertension. What is the mechanism of this drug?
choices: Activation of prostacyclin receptors, raising cAMP
Stimulation of soluble guanylate cyclase, raising cGMP
questions.explanation: A continuous IV infusion with **flushing**, headache, diarrhea, **jaw pain** and **rebound** on abrupt stop is **epoprostenol**, a **prostacyclin** that acts on IP receptors, raises **cAMP**, dilates pulmonary vessels and inhibits platelets. Its very short half-life explains both the need for continuous infusion and the rebound. Sildenafil (PDE-5 inhibition) is tempting because it also causes flushing and headache, but it is usually taken by mouth, does not cause jaw pain and raises cGMP, not cAMP.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma infusão IV contínua com **rubor**, cefaleia, diarreia, **dor na mandíbula** e **rebote** na suspensão abrupta corresponde ao **epoprostenol**, uma **prostaciclina** que age nos receptores IP, aumenta o **AMPc**, dilata os vasos pulmonares e inibe as plaquetas. Sua meia-vida muito curta explica tanto a necessidade de infusão contínua quanto o rebote. A sildenafila (inibição da PDE-5) é tentadora porque também causa rubor e cefaleia, mas costuma ser usada por via oral, não causa dor na mandíbula e aumenta o GMPc, e não o AMPc.
